title: Goldman Sachs Backs Nvidia as GTC Reinforces AI Deployment Momentum; Morgan Stanley Lifts Brent Forecast to $90
text:

 Add preferred source Goldman Sachs maintained its "Buy" rating and $300 price target on Nvidia following the company's Berlin GTC event, saying that while the presentation had limited immediate impact on the stock, it reinforced the view that AI deployment continues apace, and highlighted plans to expand substrate capacity to 2.5x and CoWoS-R capacity to 3x. Morgan Stanley, citing a concentrated release of refinery maintenance pressure, expects refined product tightness to persist until mid-2027 and raised its Q4 2027 Brent crude forecast to $90 a barrel from $75; Deutsche Bank offered a wide range of $74 to $130, with the key variable being whether shipping through the Strait of Hormuz can normalize. On individual stocks, Goldman Sachs gave a positive assessment of Tesla's third-quarter gross margin beat but maintained a Neutral rating, while Deutsche Bank recommended buying Netflix on weakness. Key Elements 
 Goldman Sachs Nvidia Morgan Stanley Brent Crude Deutsche Bank Tesla CoreWeave SpaceX UBS Netflix Strait of Hormuz Several foreign investment banks published research reports in quick succession around October 21, with Goldman Sachs' observations on Nvidia's Berlin GTC event and Morgan Stanley's latest pricing on diesel and crude oil supply drawing the most market attention. Goldman Sachs maintained its "Buy" rating and $300 price target on Nvidia, arguing that while the presentation had limited immediate effect in lifting the stock, it further solidified the judgment that AI deployment continues to advance.
 Goldman Sachs noted that the unit economics of existing data center projects at cloud giants and neocloud providers remain supportive, and that Nvidia is helping customers deploy through capacity expansion, compressed deployment cycles and efficiency gains, while also strengthening the security of enterprise AI agents and expanding revenue sources from physical AI.
 On capacity, Nvidia and its partners plan to raise related substrate capacity to 2.5x over the coming years, expand Amkor's CoWoS-R capacity to 3x, and scale up testing and co-packaged optics capacity in tandem. Goldman Sachs interpreted this as Nvidia preparing for a larger CPU ramp than previously expected.
 Nvidia's DSX POD program, expected to launch in early 2027, uses pre-assembled Vera Rubin rack modules that can be shipped as a whole, with the goal of compressing deployment time from several months to two weeks. The company said its DSX Factory platform can cut power consumption on a 2GW project by about 30% and save 56 million liters of water per day. OpenShell moves critical permission controls outside the agent, combining Vera Rubin, Vera CPU and BlueField-4 DPU to enforce security policies in hardware.
 In physical AI, the footprint spans autonomous driving, robotaxi, humanoid robots and telecom infrastructure, with related revenue reaching $11 billion (about NT$360 billion) in the first half of fiscal 2027, roughly 30% higher than all of fiscal 2026. Goldman Sachs also flagged the support from about $235 billion (about NT$7.6 trillion) in authorized buybacks, while cautioning that slower AI spending, intensifying competition and supply constraints are the main risks.
 Diesel Tightness May Persist Into Mid-2027; Morgan Stanley Raises Oil Forecast 
 Morgan Stanley's October 20 report focused on refined products. The bank argued that pressure from delayed refinery maintenance is being released in concentrated fashion, and that even if some unplanned outages resume operations, the refined products market could remain tight until mid-2027, prompting it to raise its Q4 2027 Brent crude price forecast to $90 a barrel from $75.
 The report noted that combined refinery throughput in Russia and the Middle East fell about 3 million barrels per day year-on-year in September, with seaborne refined product exports down by a similar magnitude—roughly a tenth of global seaborne supply of those products. Drone attacks on Russian refineries and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz leave the recovery outlook highly uncertain.
 High margins have prompted other refiners to postpone maintenance, but delays ultimately have limits. Known plans show that global maintenance-related capacity will rise from about 3 million barrels per day in Q4 2026 to 6.4 million barrels per day in Q2 2027, an increment about 2.5 times the normal level. Morgan Stanley estimates global throughput will then be about 81 million barrels per day, 1 million to 2 million barrels per day below market consensus.
 European diesel inventories are expected to keep declining. Even assuming a resumption of net imports of 150,000 barrels per day from November, commercial stocks could still fall to 130 million barrels by November 2027, below the record low of 134 million barrels set in 2018. The bank believes the upside in diesel prices is largely reflected, but that the forward curve implies too rapid a decline, with the opportunity lying more in forward time spreads; its model shows the ICE diesel front-month versus second-month spread could widen to $70 to $80 per metric ton in Q2 2027, versus about $30 currently for the corresponding adjacent months around mid-2027.
 On crude, attacks on commercial vessels around the strait rose from 2 to 4 per week in the summer to 7 to 12 recently, with oil flows down about 4 million barrels per day from recent highs. Morgan Stanley still uses $75 a barrel as its long-term price anchor but believes a return will take longer.
 Deutsche Bank offered a wider range, saying Brent crude could head toward either $74 or $130 a barrel in 2027, with the key being whether the Middle East conflict and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz can normalize—a $56 gap between the two scenarios. The bank noted that vessel attacks in the Middle East rose to their highest level since the war began in October, that the number of incidents confirmed by the International Maritime Organization could double this month, and that charter costs for very large crude carriers from the Arabian Gulf to the Mediterranean have doubled from $16 to $32 a barrel.
 Deutsche Bank estimates that the global oil supply-demand balance will swing from a surplus of 1.7 million barrels per day in 2025 to a deficit of 1.8 million barrels per day in 2026; if shipping through the strait normalizes, it would flip to a surplus of 4.1 million barrels per day in 2027. In its base case, negotiations produce a ceasefire and push broader dialogue, bringing Brent to $74 in 2027, about a third below current levels; if the war continues into next year, prices could rise toward $130.
 Tesla Gross Margin Beats; Deutsche Bank Says Buy Netflix 
 On individual stocks, Goldman Sachs gave an initially positive assessment of Tesla's third-quarter results, saying autonomous driving, orders and gross margin performance should be recognized by investors, but that elevated operating expenses, energy revenue below expectations and Optimus still iterating kept it at "Neutral" with a 12-month price target of $360. Tesla's third-quarter revenue was $28.046 billion (about NT$910 billion), essentially flat year-on-year and in line with FactSet consensus; adjusted earnings per share were $0.48, above the $0.45 expected. Overall gross margin was 19.6%, and automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits was 18.1%, both beating expectations.
 However, higher operating expenses and lower credit revenue left operating income at just $718 million (about NT$23 billion), below both Goldman Sachs and FactSet expectations. Third-quarter free cash flow was $1.531 billion (about NT$50 billion), and capital expenditure was $4.7 billion (about NT$150 billion), below Goldman Sachs' forecast of $8 billion (about NT$260 billion). Active FSD subscribers reached 1.74 million, up 18% quarter-on-quarter and 67% year-on-year; FSD take rates on new vehicle deliveries in North America exceeded 75%, up from more than 55% in the second quarter.
 Deutsche Bank maintained its "Buy" rating on Netflix. The bank argued that aside from some delay in executing its advertising strategy, Netflix's third-quarter results revealed no new negative catalysts, and that the roughly 5% post-earnings share decline was an overreaction; it trimmed its price target to $93 from $95 on slightly lower earnings forecasts. Netflix's third-quarter revenue was $12.874 billion (about NT$420 billion) and adjusted earnings per share were $0.87, while $4.8 billion (about NT$160 billion) of buybacks set a quarterly record. The revenue adjustment stemmed mainly from advertising revenue coming in about $300 million short of the original $3 billion target, with growth slowing from 100% to 80%, which Deutsche Bank attributed to execution delays rather than a change in the long-term trajectory.
 On the AI compute leasing side, Goldman Sachs broke down CoreWeave's financing needs, calculating that after including funding sources such as customer prepayments, about $19.5 billion to $23 billion (about NT$630 billion to NT$750 billion) in new debt would be needed to fulfill existing orders, depending on GPU useful-life assumptions; it maintained a "Buy" rating and $106 price target. As of August, CoreWeave's backlog stood at $129 billion (about NT$4.2 trillion).
 JPMorgan's well-known analyst Doug Anmuth doubled his SpaceX price target to $500 from $240, implying upside of more than 200% based on Wednesday's close of $159.31. He argued that SpaceX holds a first-mover and dominant position in a potential market expected to exceed $28 trillion, with ambitions spanning an interplanetary species, space-based AI compute, lunar bases and the construction of cities on other planets.
 UBS, meanwhile, is bullish on the growth opportunities in embodied intelligence, noting that advances in compute and AI are pushing technology from the digital world into physical applications, with humanoid robots, assisted driving and robotaxis poised to become high-growth areas. The bank contrasted AI progress roughly doubling every seven months with Moore's Law's 18-to-24-month doubling of compute, stressing that technological evolution is accelerating, and recommended broad coverage across humanoid robots, advanced driver-assistance systems, robotaxis, as well as industrial automation, agritech, smart glasses, robotic surgery and drones.
 Market Impact 
 Overall, this round of foreign bank reports sent fairly divergent signals. On the AI theme, Goldman Sachs gave a positive assessment of Nvidia's capacity expansion and deployment efficiency, and argued that solid earnings, lighter positioning and lower valuations should help support equities through year-end, but its risk-appetite indicator turned negative for the first time since March, with sentiment and positioning gauges falling to their lowest since April, suggesting growing investor doubts about the financing and returns of AI capital expenditure.
 The energy signal leans toward tightness. Morgan Stanley and Deutsche Bank both identified the Strait of Hormuz situation as the biggest variable for oil prices, warning that forward-curve pricing for diesel and crude may face re-rating, putting pressure on shipping, aviation and other transport-cost-sensitive industries; conversely, if shipping through the strait normalizes, the supply-demand balance could quickly flip to surplus, leaving considerable downside for oil prices as well. For investors, valuation divergence among AI-related stocks and two-way tail risks in energy prices will be the two main themes for asset allocation before year-end.
